Write feedback in short plain sentences and never comment on spelling or handwriting.

Question 12(b) [4 marks]: Explain the influence that variety and variation in demand would have on the operations processes of this business.
STIMULUS / CASE INFORMATION:
A business sells ice-creams and enjoys a prime position on a popular beach front. Sales have increased on weekends and school holidays due to a viral social media post highlighting the large selection of flavours and toppings.

MARKING CRITERIA (out of 4):
4 marks: Makes the relationships clear between the influence that variety and variation in demand has on the operations processes of this business
3 marks: Makes the relationships clear between the influence that variety OR variation in demand has on the operations processes of this business but only sketches in general terms the other relationship
2 marks: Sketches in general terms the influence of variety and variation in demand OR makes the relationships clear between the influence that variety OR variation in demand has on the operations processes of this business
1 marks: Makes a relevant statement about variety or variation in demand

SAMPLE ANSWER (official):
Variety refers to the number of different models and variations offered by a business in its products or services. Increased variety can have a number of impacts on the inputs used by this business, specifically the transformed inputs. For example, a much broader range of raw materials would be needed, and these complicate the storage and transformation process trying to avoid cross contamination. Variation in demand is looking at how fluctuations in customer demand would impact on operations processes, for example weekends and holidays for this business. This would impact their inputs, specifically their transforming resources and facilities: due to the number and range of different flavours this could require careful manufacturing layout configuration, different production lines, and different types of specialised equipment to produce different batches of flavours.

ANSWERS COULD INCLUDE (the student does not need every point):
Variety: different raw materials to manage, order and store (cross contamination); different recipes (information); different production methods needing different skills; extensive space, production lines and specialised equipment; slower, more skilled customer service (advice on flavours, allergens). Variation in demand: stock up on raw materials before weekends and school holidays; more labour (transforming input) for peak periods; a more efficient product layout or a reconfigured process layout for peaks (for example takeaway only, more queuing space); more staff serving simultaneously.

TEACHER MARKER COMMENTS:
Most students understood what variety and variation in demand are. However, when linking to operations processes, many linked back to the business at a macro level or to financial considerations (revenue, profits, sales), which is not what the question was looking for. When answering an operations question, your answer needs to be full of operations terminology and concepts from the syllabus.
